_comment_gates: prompt/image/mesh = stop for your approval after that pipeline stage. vision = render-vision gate, one of off | focused | full: after an action the assistant renders the scene and looks at it before claiming anything visual. focused (default) covers animation, rig/mesh binding, brush placement and spawns; full adds every other look-changing step including raw bpy. Each check costs one extra vision call.
_comment_providers: Every seat (orchestrator, troubleshooter, metaprompter, vision, utility) picks WHO answers via seats.<name>.provider: claude-cli = your Claude Code CLI login (default, no key); openai-compat + endpoint 'local' = a local OpenAI-compatible server such as LM Studio or llama.cpp (no key); openai-compat + endpoint 'openai' = OpenAI with your API key. 'utility' is the small model that picks a category for a prop (default Sonnet). API keys live in .secrets/providers.json (set them in Settings -> General -> Seats) and NEVER in this file; endpoints.openai only names the URL and which key to use. For local servers Phoenix turns thinking off by default (a thinking model otherwise returns empty answers); add seats.<name>.options to pass extra request fields. ChatGPT subscription: provider 'codex-cli' runs your own ChatGPT plan (Plus/Pro) through the Codex CLI - install it (npm install -g @openai/codex), run `codex login` once in a terminal, then pick 'ChatGPT plan (Codex CLI)' in Settings -> General -> Seats; an empty model = Codex's default; if Phoenix cannot find the binary set apps.codex to its full path. Businesses should use the OpenAI API key path instead. The vision seat can be any model that passes the vision test (Settings -> General). A seat without 'provider' keeps working: a model named claude* uses the CLI, anything else the local server.
_comment_seats_vision: The model that LOOKS at renders (inspect_render + the render-vision gate). It is a judge, not an orchestrator: it is the only thing that can contradict a 'fixed' claim, so it gets its own seat. Remove this seat and it falls back to the orchestrator's model - which means changing the orchestrator would silently change the judge too. Keep them separate on purpose.
_comment_endpoints: comfyui = the ComfyUI running your image, mesh AND i2i/edit workflows. 8188 is ComfyUI's own default port; change it if you started ComfyUI with --port. Running ONE ComfyUI with all nodes? Leave just this endpoint and everything runs there. Running SEVERAL (common — Trellis and Qwen-Image-Edit/Flux need incompatible CUDA/Python, so separate venvs on separate ports, on one machine or several)? Also set the OPTIONAL comfyui_bild = the second ComfyUI endpoint that i2i workflows tagged instance:'bild' use. Note: instances on one GPU share its VRAM. local = an optional OpenAI-compatible local model server (e.g. LM Studio) for the metaprompter. OPTIONAL rigSsh + comfySupervisor: only if your ComfyUI runs on ANOTHER host managed by a supervisor over SSH — then Phoenix can restart it when it's down. Omit both on a local setup; Phoenix just tells you to start ComfyUI instead.
_comment_hyMotion: Text->Motion, optional. api = the ComfyUI that has ComfyUI-HY-Motion1 in custom_nodes and the weights under models/HY-Motion/. That can be the same ComfyUI as endpoints.comfyui (then leave both alike) or a separate one; what matters is that the nodes are installed there, not which port it uses. Point it at another machine (e.g. http://gpu-box.local:8188) if generation runs on a separate GPU box. template = a Mixamo REST-POSE (T-pose) FBX, relative to that ComfyUI's folder; create it with scripts/hy-motion/make_tpose_char.py.
_comment_voice: Voice AND SFX tabs, optional. api = a CrispASR speech server (start it with: crispasr --server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090 -m tada --voice-dir <folder of .gguf voice packs>). Leave empty to hide those tabs' functions. It may run on another machine - point it there (e.g. http://gpu-box.local:8090); generation belongs where the GPU is. ffmpeg = path to an ffmpeg binary; the voice EFFECTS and every SFX edit/bench render need it; leave empty to auto-detect the one bundled with imageio-ffmpeg, and if that finds nothing the effects fail with a clear error. A voice pack is baked once with `crispasr --make-ref` from a reference recording - reference quality is output quality, and the pack also freezes the delivery, so record calm and clean unless you want that colour in every line. ENGINE PICKER: CrispASR is the integrated default and works against a plain CrispASR server. The other engines in the picker (Chatterbox, CosyVoice) route through a voice-service dispatcher that is NOT part of this release, so they ship greyed out ('requires the voice-service dispatcher - coming in a future version') unless you set voice.dispatcher = true (only meaningful if your voice.api actually runs that dispatcher).
_comment_comfyInstall: OPTIONAL. Enables the Workflow library's '⬇ Acquire' button to fetch a workflow's missing models / custom nodes for you. Shape: one key per ComfyUI instance name -> { root, via }. root = the ComfyUI checkout on the target machine (models land in root/models, custom nodes in root/custom_nodes). via = 'local' (default - install straight onto THIS machine, the normal single-machine case) or 'supervisor' (install on another host over endpoints.rigSsh - only for a remote/supervised ComfyUI). LEFT EMPTY (or a workflow's instance absent): Acquire shows 'manual' and you place files yourself - never a silent install to some default location. WHICH KEY? image and mesh workflows (Flux/SD/Trellis - no explicit instance) resolve under the instance name 'trellis', so a single-machine user sets comfyInstall.trellis = { "root": "<your ComfyUI folder>", "via": "local" }. i2i workflows tagged instance:'bild' use comfyInstall.bild. Example (single machine): { "trellis": { "root": "/home/you/ComfyUI", "via": "local" } }.
_comment_voiceInstall: OPTIONAL. Same idea as comfyInstall, for downloadable voice engines: one key per voice instance name (there is only one voice endpoint today, so the key is 'voice') -> { root, via }. root = the engine/bench root on the target machine (a venv lands at root/<engine venv path>, a git+requirements engine's repo at root/<engine id>, weights under root/<relative weights dir>). via = 'local' (default) or 'supervisor' (over endpoints.rigSsh). Absent -> Acquire shows 'manual' for voice engines, never a silent install. Note: the downloadable engines also need voice.dispatcher (see _comment_voice) to be usable at all in this release. PLATFORM: a voice-engine Acquire runs its venv/pip/git steps on a Linux/macOS (POSIX) target - and cancelling a via:'local' voice acquire on a WINDOWS host may not stop the in-flight step (Windows has no process-group kill), unlike the portable ComfyUI Acquire. Example: { "voice": { "root": "/home/you/tts-bench", "via": "local" } }.
_comment_feedback: Optional. Set endpointUrl to a URL that accepts a JSON POST and the in-app Feedback form posts there; leave empty and the form stays hidden.
_comment_preflight: What `node preflight.js` compares the ComfyUI environment against. Drift is reported as a warning, not an error - set these to whatever your working install reports.
_comment_apps: blender = full path to your Blender executable, used only so Phoenix can launch it for you; optional. Windows: C:\\Program Files\\Blender Foundation\\Blender 5.1\\blender.exe - macOS: /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender - Linux: /usr/bin/blender. blenderIpcDir (not listed above, optional) = the folder Phoenix and the Blender addon exchange commands through. WARNING: setting it here only moves the PHOENIX side - the addon reads the PHOENIX_BLENDER_IPC_DIR environment variable and nothing else, so unless you ALSO start Blender with that variable set to the same path, every Blender call will time out. Leave it unset unless you know you need it. comfyOutput = the folder ComfyUI writes generated files into. Left empty, Phoenix looks in ~/Documents/ComfyUI/output, which is where ComfyUI-Desktop puts them - a portable or git install writes somewhere else, so SET THIS to <your ComfyUI folder>/output or the mesh stage will fail to collect a mesh that generated fine.
_comment_unreal: The Unreal bridge (place brushes / spawn characters into a running editor, pull assets back to Blender, screenshot the viewport) - Phoenix NEVER starts Unreal, you keep the editor open. unrealEngine = folder of your Unreal install, e.g. C:\\Program Files\\Epic Games\\UE_5.8; optional, left empty Phoenix takes the newest UE_* it can find. python = a real Python 3 the bridge helper runs; leave empty to use `python` from PATH, but on Windows avoid the Microsoft-Store stub (it exits instantly and every Unreal action fails). In the editor: enable the Python Editor Script Plugin and tick Project Settings -> Python -> Enable Remote Execution.
_comment_checkpoints: A copy of the open Blender scene is saved before each step that changes it (in chat and over MCP, taken right where Blender is touched, e.g. a generated mesh right before its import; the Library and Human-tab buttons do not take one yet apart from that import), so you can rewind. enabled = on/off (the checkbox in the gear panel); keep = how many copies to keep (1-100); maxGB = disk budget for them (0.1-100). Keep and the budget are set in Settings -> General.
_comment_mcp: Phoenix as a tool for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor (node phoenix-mcp.js, see README). allowBlenderRun = also offer blender_run (arbitrary Python in your open Blender scene) to those agents; off by default. allowUnrealRun = also offer unreal_run (arbitrary Python in a running Unreal Editor). allowDelete = also offer delete_asset / delete_brush / delete_material (permanent - a checkpoint cannot bring them back). All three are off by default; toggle them in Settings -> Connections.
_comment_remesh: OPTIONAL, paid. Remesh a staged GLB through Meshy (meshy.ai, cloud): Phoenix UPLOADS the mesh and it costs Meshy credits (about 5 per remesh; a Meshy plan with API access is needed). Off by default - tick 'Allow uploading meshes to Meshy' in Settings -> Connections and store your Meshy API key there (it goes to .secrets/, never to this file). topology = quad | triangle and targetPolycount = 100-300000 are the defaults the Library's Remesh dialog opens with (it remembers your last choice); maxUploadMB = largest GLB Phoenix will upload. In chat it runs only in Auto mode; the Library has a 'Remesh via Meshy' button for one-off use.
